If x,y take distinct colors a,b and A,B count their external common neighbors of those colors, strict unique plurality would require A>B+1 and B>A+1, contradiction. Consequently each clique has constant color, and each vertex sees (s-1)+s*t_own same-colored neighbors versus s*t_other of a competing color; for integers and s>=2, strict inequality iff t_own>=t_other, proving size-independent reduction to weak plurality on H. On base degree-one/two paths and cycles weak plurality iff every nonconstant color run length >=2, with endpoints constrained; compositions of n into r lengths>=2 give C(n-r-1,r-1) for paths, and marked cyclic boundaries give (n/r)C(n-r-1,r-1) for cycles; appropriate proper run color factors establish exact formulas, n=1 isolated case q and components product. Independent brute named-color enumeration on eight small path/cycle blowups, including s=3, agrees. General true-twin theorem and unbounded closed sums are deductive, not extrapolated from brute force.
